defects.claim_says: Section 1 quoted ending '...to aid the civil authorities of the District of \nstatus to aid civil authorities of the District of Columbia.' with no mention of any correction; the rationale describes the number-search hits as 'two source-ladder queue files created for EO 10030'.
defects.source_says: One of those held files is the Federal Register correction at 34 FR 15443 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10030_Executive_Order_11485_correction_34_FR_15443_PDF_page_5_7fb95ff9e4.txt), which states that the last sentence of Section 1 as printed at 34 FR 15411 should read '...to aid the civil authorities of the District of Columbia.' The 1989 codification SOURCE line cites 34 FR 15411, 15443. The genuine claim still quotes the misprinted line as the operative text and leaves this held FR correction unaddressed and misdescribed.

evidence_checked: genuine claim diffed against the blind version: only operative_clauses[4].first_end.date differs (1969-10-01)
reasoning: The genuine version corrects the planted date: section 5 now ends on 1969-10-01, the signing and filing date, which matches the held FR text and the claim's reasons. Everything else is identical to the blind version, so the second defect I recorded blind remains: the held FR correction at 34 FR 15443, which rewrites the last sentence of section 1, is neither cited nor addressed. The claim quotes the misprinted sentence as the operative text and describes the correction file only as a queue file for EO 10030. Under the rule that every held Federal Register note on the order must be addressed, the genuine claim is rejected. Adding the correction as the corrected wording of section 1, and accurately describing the file, would cure it; the status (yes) is not in doubt.
